data.body:
Fixes bug Bca3a5c599c: CI publish.yml verify step 'upgrade-dry-run --previous-release --build-old --confirmations-ok' (clone at 3720a2105a, 62937 events, 266 shards, stamps 0.1.10..0.2.2) FAILS: steps 1,2,3,5,8,9,10 pass; step 4 'apply with a snapshot, again, restore' FAIL 'doctor after the apply exited 1: ...which is abandoned and will never be done, so AI-roles is stuck for good: ddflow update AI-roles --needs CN-manifest,CN-projects-toml / 67 problem(s).'; step 6 'MCP connect' FAIL 'doctor after the consent exited 1'; step 7 'two agents, one task' FAIL 'doctor exited 1'. Final 'dry run FAIL: 11 check(s)'. Hypothesis: the 67 problems are pre-existing in the old queue; the absolute doctor-exit-0 assertion measures old queue hygiene, not the upgrade; needs differential before/after check.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bca3a5c599c --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bca3a5c599c --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug Bca3a5c599c: publish verify: upgrade dry-run fails on previous release's pre-existing doctor problems

evidence.note: research note recorded: CONFIRMED, 67 pre-existing stuck edges on 3720a2105a with the new doctor, 0 on main
ddflow brief decisions/rules reviewed; D-dry-run-from-running-version kept (clone from previous release), only the doctor assertion changed
Rehearsal.doctor_verdict differential vs baseline; 3 new tests; dry run PASS 11 checks locally

data.claim: The dry run's red doctor assertions are the previous release's own 67 stuck-behind-abandoned-prerequisite problems, flagged by a doctor check the old binary lacks; they exist before any apply
data.falsifier: new doctor on an untouched clone of 3720a2105a reports 0 problems
data.mechanism: stuck_edges in the new doctor sees 67 needs-edges onto abandoned *-decide items in the 3720a2105a log
data.probe_output: 67 problems, all needs X which is abandoned; main clone: 0; dry-run diag: dry-read doctor already exit 1 before any apply
data.question: Why does the publish dry run fail on doctor?

chunk_findings.detail: The new doctor invocations pass `--json` **before** the `doctor` subcommand: `self.ddflow(self.new, repo, "--json", "doctor", ...)`. In the same file’s unchanged upgrade call the JSON flag is passed **after** the subcommand (`self.ddflow(self.new, repo, "upgrade", "--plan", "--json", ...)`), so `--json` is a `doctor` subcommand option, not a main/global one. With a standard subcommand parser, `--json doctor` is rejected as an unrecognized argument, the command exits 2 with a usage message, `doctor_problems` returns `None`, `doctor_baseline` is set to `None`, and every `doctor_verdict` then fails with the “no baseline”/“no readable report” error. The dry run therefore still fails on the same pre-existing 67 problems this change is meant to ignore.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_dryrun.py:770 and :779

chunk_findings.detail: The function only removes dynamic text after a spaced em dash. Doctor problem lines without an em dash (such as the bug’s `... ddflow update AI-roles --needs CN-manifest,CN-projects-toml / 67 problem(s)` or the fixture `OLD[1]`) keep their trailing counts and paths in the identity. Given before `"stuck: AI-roles needs CN-manifest, which is abandoned and will never be done / 67 problem(s)"` and after the same line with `/ 68 problem(s)` (no new doctor problem, only a count changed), `problem_identity` returns two different strings, so `new_problems` reports the after version as NEW and the dry-run fails on the previous release’s pre-existing hygiene — the exact failure this change is meant to suppress.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_dryrun.py:problem_identity

chunk_findings.detail: The contested-record filter uses substring membership, `c.split()[-1] in p`, rather than token/record equality. With `before=set()`, `after=["decision D-110 is CONTESTED"]`, and `contested=["decision D-11"]`, `c.split()[-1]` is `"D-11"`, which is a substring of `"D-110"`, so `" is CONTESTED" in p` is true and the new problem is filtered out. That incorrectly turns a genuinely added unexpected contested problem into a pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_dryrun.py:new_problems

chunk_findings.detail: The new invocations still pass `--json` before the subcommand: `self.ddflow(self.new, repo, "--json", "doctor", ...)`. The same file’s known-good upgrade invocation passes it after the subcommand (`"upgrade", "--plan", "--json"`), so the doctor parser is the place that consumes `--json`. With a subcommand parser, `--json doctor` is rejected as an unrecognized argument, `doctor` exits 2 with a usage message, `doctor_problems` returns `None`, `doctor_baseline` caches `None`, and every `doctor_verdict` then returns `"doctor could not be read on the untouched clone, so there is no baseline"`. The CI run from the bug still fails on steps 4/6/7 even with zero upgrade-added problems.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_dryrun.py:doctor_baseline,doctor_verdict

chunk_findings.detail: This still matches the reported failure: the function only strips dynamic text after a spaced em dash. The bug’s doctor line has no em dash (`...ddflow update AI-roles --needs CN-manifest,CN-projects-toml / 67 problem(s)`), so the trailing `/ 67 problem(s)` remains part of the identity. A count-only change from `/ 67 problem(s)` to `/ 68 problem(s)` therefore appears as a new problem in `new_problems` and the dry run fails for a non-upgrade issue, so the core bug is not actually fixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_dryrun.py:problem_identity

chunk_findings.detail: The contested-record filter still uses substring membership (`c.split()[-1] in p`) rather than exact token/record equality. For example, `before=set()`, `after=["decision D-110 is CONTESTED"]`, and `contested=["decision D-11"]` makes `"D-11"` match inside `"D-110"`, so `" is CONTESTED" in p` is true and the genuinely added unexpected contested problem is filtered out. That turns an upgrade-induced regression into a pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_dryrun.py:new_problems

chunk_findings.detail: `problem_identity` removes trailing counts and paths only when the line contains the exact spaced em dash ` \u2014 `. The bug’s own pre-existing problem line has no such dash, e.g. before: `"stuck: AI-roles needs CN-manifest, which is abandoned and will never be done / 67 problem(s)"` and after the upgrade the same pre-existing item reports `"… / 68 problem(s)"`. Since only the aggregate count changed, `problem_identity(before)` and `problem_identity(after)` differ only in that count, so `new_problems` reports the pre-existing problem as newly added and the dry-run still fails on the exact Bca3a5c599c input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_dryrun.py:problem_identity

chunk_findings.detail: The new invocations still pass `--json` before the `doctor` subcommand: `self.ddflow(self.new, repo, "--json", "doctor", agent=...)`. The unchanged upgrade invocation in the same file passes the same flag after the subcommand (`upgrade --plan --json`), so `--json` is a subcommand option. On the targeted upgrade, `ddflow --json doctor` is rejected with a usage error, `doctor_problems` gets no JSON, `doctor_baseline` returns `None`, and every `doctor_verdict` fails with `"doctor could not be read on the untouched clone..."`. This FUILDING is the exact failure from Bca3a5c599c reborn.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_dryrun.py:doctor_baseline and doctor_verdict

chunk_findings.detail: The identity function still only removes dynamic text after a spaced em dash. A pre-existing problem line without an em dash, such as `"... ddflow update AI-roles --needs CN-manifest,CN-projects-toml / 67 problem(s)"`, keeps its trailing `/ 67 problem(s)` count in the identity. Before and after the upgrade the same record with `/ 68 problem(s)` has a different identity, so `new_problems` reports a new problem when only the count changed, and the dry-run still fails.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_dryrun.py:problem_identity

chunk_findings.detail: The contested-record filter still uses substring membership, `c.split()[-1] in p`, rather than token/record equality. With `before=set()`, `after=["decision D-110 is CONTESTED"]`, and `contested=["decision D-11"]`, `c.split()[-1]` is `"D-11"`, which is a substring of `"D-110"`. The genuinely added unexpected contested problem is filtered out and the dry-run falsely passes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_dryrun.py:new_problems

chunk_findings.detail: `run_cli(repo, "--json", "doctor")` puts `--json` before the `doctor` subcommand. In this CLI `--json` is a subcommand option, not a top-level global option; the unchanged upgrade call in `ddflow/services/upgrade_dryrun.py` passes it after the subcommand. The call should be `run_cli(repo, "doctor", "--json")`. As written, the command exits with a usage error, `out` is not JSON, `doctor_problems` cannot parse it, and the changed test fails even when the production bug is fixed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_upgrade_plan_contested.py:106

chunk_findings.detail: `changed` changes only `OLD[0]`, whose dynamic suffix follows an em dash; `OLD[1]` (the no-em-dash problem line from the bug) is copied verbatim. A broken `problem_identity` that strips only after `" — "` still makes this test pass. The actual bug input is the same no-em-dash line changing from `/ 67 problem(s)` to `/ 68 problem(s)`; the test never supplies that case, so it does not fail on the unfixed code for the no-em-dash path.

Elsewhere in this file the known-good invocation is `"upgrade", "--plan", "--json"`, i.e. `--json` is consumed by the subcommand parser. chunk_findings.detail: The contested-record filter still uses substring membership (`c.split()[-1] in p`) rather than exact record/token equality. chunk_findings.detail: The identity is `line.split(" \u2014 ")[0]`, so trailing counts/paths are removed only for lines containing a spaced em dash. The bug’s pre-existing doctor line has no em dash: `ddflow update AI-roles --needs CN-manifest,CN-projects-toml / 67 problem(s)`. If the same pre-existing item is reported after the upgrade with `/ 68 problem(s)`, `problem_identity` keeps the count in both identities, so `new_problems` treats `/ 68 problem(s)` as absent from `before`. `doctor_verdict` then reports an upgrade-caused problem, and the dry run still fails on previous-release doctor problems.
